_readme: LITERARY TEXTS - poems, short stories, plays and novels.
Every text on RCF English is set out in the SAME fifteen sections, so students
always know where to look, and everything belonging to one text stays together.
TO ADD A TEXT:
1. Copy _src/pages/_template-literature-text.json to a new file in
_src/pages/ol-literature/texts/ (or al-literature/texts/).
2. Fill in the fifteen sections in that page file.
3. Add a short entry to the list below so the text appears in the genre
listings and in site search. The 'slug' must match the page's slug.
4. Run build.cmd.
COPYRIGHT - THIS MATTERS.
Do NOT reproduce a complete copyrighted poem, story, play or novel, or a
large part of one, without written permission. Summaries, analysis, themes,
character notes, questions and model answers written by RCF English are your
own work and may be published freely. Short quotations may be used for
study and criticism; keep them short and always name the author.
NEVER invent a quotation, a plot detail, a date or a fact about an author.
If you are not certain of a quotation, check the text before publishing it.
FIELDS:  slug (the page address), title, author, genre (poetry | short-story |
drama | novel), level (O/L or A/L), summary (a list of short
paragraphs), published.
Texts such as Twilight of a Crane and Bringing Tony Home are added here in
exactly this way once their pages have been written and checked.
